AbstainReason.description:
Why a branch declined to vote, or why the whole bundle abstained.

These are *outcomes*, not errors. They never map to an HTTP error status and
never render as a failure in the UI. Contrast with ``ErrorCode``.
AbstainReason.title: AbstainReason

Artifact.description:
A rendered explanation, stored out of band and referenced by URL.

Never inlined as base64 — a bundle must stay small enough to cache cheaply.

ref.title: Ref

caption.description: User-facing caption. For GRADCAM this MUST read as attribution ('regions that most influenced this score'), never as localisation.
caption.title: Caption

BranchId.description: Evidence sources. ``C`` is intentionally absent — see module docstring.
BranchId.title: BranchId

BranchResult.description:
One evidence source's contribution.

``logit`` is stored at full precision and must never be rounded before
persistence. Rounding collapses distinct saturated scores into ties, which
silently perturbs AUC and breaks the monotonic relationship between logit
and p_fake that calibration depends on.

logit.description: Raw pre-calibration logit. Full precision, never rounded. For branch P this is a one-sided authenticity credit and MUST be >= 0 — absence of provenance contributes exactly zero, never positive evidence of manipulation.
logit.title: Logit

weight.description: Fusion coefficient applied. Null when the branch did not score.
weight.title: Weight

coherent.title: Coherent

FaceTrack.description:
One identity across the analysed frames.

**What actually publishes these today, stated plainly because three other
artifacts imply otherwise:**

* **Images** yield exactly one track — the largest detected face, whose
  verdict is published as the whole image's. That is a policy the product
  chose for single-subject media, not a property of images; it is R16 and it
  is open.
* **Video yields none at all.** ``VideoPipeline`` runs no face detection, so
  every video bundle carries ``faces=[]`` and a null ``quality.face_px``.
  That is R18. The fixtures and the stub handlers depict a populated track
  because they describe the post-SCRFD target the frontend builds against.
* **``bbox`` is the detector's box, not the region the model scored.**
  ``crop_face`` expands it by the selection policy's margin, then clips it
  to the image — a different, and usually larger, window than what is
  published here. No field on this contract carries that window;
  recovering it requires re-deriving it from ``bbox`` and the shipped
  ``FaceSelectionPolicy``, which a client cannot do from the wire alone.
  That gap is R26, open.

``frames_seen`` is therefore always 1 in practice; a value above 1 belongs to
the tracked video path that does not exist yet.

status.description: Set when this track abstained; null when it scored.

QualityReport.description:
Input quality, and the gate's decision.

This is what routes low-information inputs to abstention *before* any model
votes, and what the fusion layer uses as an interaction term.

face_px.description: Short edge — min(width, height), in source pixels — of the largest detected face, where face size is FaceBox.size_px (equal to the short edge): the one metric selection, the gate and this figure all read (see docs/FACE_SIZE_POLICY.md, R20). 0 when an image has no detected face; null on every video bundle, whose path runs no face stage (R18).
face_px.title: Face Px

A contiguous run above the hysteresis threshold.

Produced by hysteresis rather than a single cut so that a curve hovering at
the boundary does not shatter into dozens of one-frame segments.

ThresholdInfo.description:
The operating point. Published so a verdict can be re-derived from p_fake.

THE BAND IS DERIVED, NEVER CONFIGURED
-------------------------------------
``band_lo`` and ``band_hi`` are outputs of ``value`` and a single width
parameter, not independent settings. They stay in the payload because
clients read them and the response schema is frozen, but every construction
is checked against the derivation, so a band that disagrees with its
threshold cannot be built — not by a factory, not by hand, and not by
deserialising a stored bundle.

Before this, the three were free to drift apart. ``decide`` compared against
``value`` first and the band second, so a configuration with
``band_hi > value`` silently truncated the band, and one with
``band_hi < value`` opened a dead zone in which scores just under the
decision boundary were reported as authentic. Both were representable and
neither was detectable from the published fields.

THE BAND STRADDLES THE THRESHOLD
--------------------------------
``band_lo < value < band_hi``, so the three regions partition [0, 1] with no
gap and no overlap:

    p <  band_lo   authentic
    p <  band_hi   insufficient evidence
    otherwise      manipulated

Note what this means for calibration: the boundary a score is actually
decided at is ``band_hi``, not ``value``. ``value`` is the calibrated centre
— the point ``threshold_at_fpr`` selects — and ``target_fpr`` is the false
positive rate *at that centre*. Because the manipulated region starts above
it, the achieved false positive rate is bounded above by ``target_fpr``
rather than equal to it, and the cost is paid in detections: scores in
``[value, band_hi)`` are calibrated as manipulated and are reported as
insufficient evidence instead.

THE BAND IS SYMMETRIC IN LOG-ODDS, NOT IN PROBABILITY
-----------------------------------------------------
This is the Batch 7 change, and it is the whole of it. The edges are

    band_lo = expit(logit(value) - margin)
    band_hi = expit(logit(value) + margin)

so the band is still *centred on its threshold* and still derived from one
number — the centring has been moved to the scale where it means something.
``margin`` is an evidence margin in log-odds: a margin of ln(1.5) says
"abstain unless the odds are at least 1.5x past the threshold odds".

Two things forced this, one mathematical and one semantic.

*Mathematical.* A band that is symmetric in probability with a width chosen
independently of the threshold **cannot exist** for every threshold: a width
of w needs ``w/2 <= min(value, 1 - value)``, so any fixed w fails once the
threshold moves within w/2 of an endpoint. That is not a hypothetical. A 2%
false-positive budget fitted on 22 negatives put the threshold at 0.9734,
where no 0.20-wide symmetric band fits, and calibration raised (R11 in the
audit). Clamping the band to [0, 1] is worse than raising: at that threshold
the clamped band is [0.8734, 1.0] and nothing is ever called manipulated
again. Log-odds symmetry has no such constraint — every finite margin around
every threshold strictly inside (0, 1) yields a valid band — so the failure
is structurally gone rather than handled.

*Semantic.* A fixed probability width is not a fixed amount of evidence.
Widening from 0.50 to 0.60 is 0.41 nats; from 0.90 to 1.00 is unbounded. The
old 0.20-wide band therefore meant something different at every threshold it
was used at, which is exactly why no value of it could be justified (R8).

``band_width`` is retained as a derived, published quantity — it is what the
risk-coverage reports read — but it is an output now, never an input.

value.description: Calibrated centre of the operating point. Always strictly inside (0, 1), since a threshold at an endpoint has no log-odds and no band can bracket it — but the bound stays [0, 1] so the published JSON Schema is unchanged; the model validator below is what rejects the endpoints.
value.title: Value

target_fpr.description: False positive rate the centre was tuned for. The achieved rate at the decision boundary (band_hi) is bounded above by this.
target_fpr.title: Target Fpr

band_lo.description: Derived: expit(logit(value) - margin). Below this, authentic. Not a setting — the band is centred on the threshold in log-odds.
band_lo.title: Band Lo

band_hi.description: Derived: expit(logit(value) + margin). At or above this, manipulated. This, not value, is the decision boundary.
band_hi.title: Band Hi

ThresholdInfo.title: ThresholdInfo

Timing.description:
Where the time went. Every field is wall clock, in milliseconds.

``queued_ms`` is time before analysis started and is therefore *outside*
``total_ms``; the three work phases are inside it. The remainder —
``total_ms`` less the phases — is fusion, calibration and bundle
construction, which are too small to be worth their own field but must not
be silently folded into one that means something else.

queued_ms.description: Submission to start of analysis. Outside total_ms.
queued_ms.title: Queued Ms

preprocess_ms.description: Decode, sampling, face detection, tensor preparation.
preprocess_ms.title: Preprocess Ms

total_ms.description: Wall clock for the whole analysis call.
total_ms.title: Total Ms

Timing.title: Timing

TopFrame.description: A frame surfaced as a thumbnail, with its own attribution artifact.

track_id.description: The faces[] track this frame's score is attributed to. **Null means no face was attributed** — which is every frame the current video path produces, because it scores whole frames and runs no face detection. A non-null value must name a track the bundle actually publishes; EvidenceBundle refuses a dangling reference.
track_id.title: Track Id

TopFrame.title: TopFrame

Verdict.description:
The three-state output. Never collapse this to a boolean.

``INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE`` is a successful result, not a failure. It is
returned when the quality gate declines the input or when no branch was able
to score it.
Verdict.title: Verdict

VideoAnalysis.description:
Present iff ``media.kind == video``.

**The current video path runs no face detection.** It samples frames,
resizes them whole to the model input, and scores them; it does not detect,
crop, track or attribute faces. So a video bundle publishes an empty
``faces[]`` and a null ``quality.face_px``, and every ``top_frames[].track_id``
is null. That is R18, and the frozen architecture's face stage for video is
SCRFD work that has not landed — see ``docs/VIDEO_FACE_SEMANTICS.md``.

The fixtures in ``contracts/fixtures.py`` deliberately depict the *target*
shape, with a populated ``FaceTrack`` and resolving track ids, because they
are what the frontend builds against. They are not a description of what the
pipeline emits today.

frames_scored.description: Sampled frames that decoded and were scored. Never exceeds frames_sampled; lower when part of a damaged clip failed to decode. See the class docstring for what this field used to claim and why that was wrong (R18).
frames_scored.title: Frames Scored

sampling.description: How frames were chosen — the ``sampling_rule`` of the ``VideoSelectionPolicy`` in force. Recorded so a result can be reproduced. The shipped value is plain uniform stride; nothing adaptive runs.
sampling.title: Sampling

pooling.description: Aggregation over frames. 'topk_mean' is the v1 baseline; 'attention' once the temporal transformer beats it by a paired-bootstrap margin.
pooling.title: Pooling

VideoAnalysis.title: VideoAnalysis

description: The single result object. Cached under ``sha256 + model.version``.

verdict.description: The three-state result for the media's single published face — the largest one detected (face_order_key selects it; see FaceTrack's own note). A multi-subject photograph's verdict describes one person in it; the platform does not currently score or publish evidence for any other face present (R16, open).

p_fake.description: Calibrated probability of manipulation. Null iff the verdict is insufficient_evidence. Stored at full precision — never round before persisting. Describes the same single selected face verdict does, not an aggregate over every face in the media.
p_fake.title: P Fake

interval.description: Uncertainty band around p_fake. Widens with branch disagreement.
interval.title: Interval

disagreement.description: Spread across scored branches. Surfaced to the user rather than collapsed — contradiction between branches is information.
disagreement.title: Disagreement
